title.narrative: Integrating MHPSS (MHFA) into Peacebuilding and Reconciliation/Emergency Response and Early Recovery

description.narrative: Nigeria continues to experience protracted conflict, displacement, and inter-communal tensions across several states where CAFOD operates. Mental health services remain significantly under-resourced, particularly in rural and conflict- affected areas. Untreated trauma and chronic psychosocial stress increase vulnerability to conflict relapse, gender-based violence(GBV), youth radicalization, and weakened social cohesion. Integrating MHPSS into existing CAFOD programming is therefore not merely a programmatic enhancement but a strategic necessity. CAFOD Nigeria and its partners have delivered highly relevant peacebuilding, livelihood, governance, and early recovery interventions across conflict-affected states. Documented reports highlight strong community engagement, effective localized delivery, and the establishment of durable structures such as peace committees, interfaith dialogue platforms, women’s cooperatives, and trauma-healing initiatives, which are ideal mechanisms for integrating structured MHPSS. These platforms demonstrate clear gains in trust-building, social cohesion, food security, and community resilience, yet they also reveal persistent psychosocial distress linked to violence, displacement, and chronic insecurity. While some trauma-healing activities exist, psychosocial support is not yet systematically integrated across program areas. Integrating MHPSS, with Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) as a foundational component, would significantly enhance the emotional and relational dimensions of peacebuilding and recovery. Training peace volunteers, interfaith leaders, cooperative heads, and emergency responders in MHFA would equip them to recognize distress, provide immediate support, and refer individuals needing specialized care. Embedding MHPSS into dialogue processes, trauma-healing centers, livelihood groups, and early-recovery activities would strengthen reconciliation, reduce conflict triggers, and reinforce community resilience.
